Building on long-term, iterative day-to-day traffic data, this study develops two advanced statistical methods to estimate the probability distribution of origin-destination demand and network flow. Initially, the probability distributions of link flow and path flow are estimated independently, after which the probability distributions of origin-destination demand and network flow are calculated using an iterative backward sampling approach. Notably, this method does not require any initial assumptions regarding the probability distribution of origin-destination demand. Furthermore, this study utilizes iterative residuals and Q-measures, also known as Hellinger distances, to assess the accuracy of the estimated probability distributions, thereby validating the results. To illustrate the efficacy of the proposed methods, this study employs a test example and two substantial network cases, showcasing the computational feasibility and accuracy of the methods.

In this study, we examine the synchronization processes occurring within a collection of oscillators with diverse frequencies and strengths of interaction. Our analysis focuses on the ordering of these oscillators as the stiffness of their connections varies, resulting in distinct states: ordered patterns and more chaotic behavior. Our findings are applicable across various contexts, including biological systems and the behavior of social groups, and can be observed through the examination of brain activity or bird migrations. We utilize both theoretical and practical approaches to understand this phenomenon, which we verify using computer simulations of a specific system featuring coupled nonlinear oscillators. Our work has potential implications for the field of applied mathematics, particularly in regards to the analysis of brain function.

The well-documented Aldous-Broder and Wilson algorithms produce spanning trees with high frequencies of occurrence, and as such, are frequently employed in computer simulations. It is established that both algorithms' results are equivalent to performing a random walk and deleting the edge that first leads to a graph that is temporally connected. This connection, in turn, is equivalent to removing edges from a temporary graph derived through the Wilson algorithm's shrinkage process, which itself generates uniform spanning trees. Consequently, this research proposes a two-stage approach for obtaining uniform spanning trees, starting with the Wilson algorithm's shrinkage process and then applying the random walk and edge deletion method on the resulting temporary graph.

This work presents a comprehensive music dataset named MusicTM-Dataset that encompasses three-core modules: audio processing, text analysis, and symbolic music interpretation. To develop this dataset, we collaborated with Music21, a widely recognized music analysis library, to gather a diverse collection of 12,000 songs, comprising 3,000 pairs of musical scores and text descriptions, along with 12,000 associated audio recordings. This dataset is designed to facilitate research in multimedia-rich music environments and serves as a essential tool for exploring cross-modal learning applications. We apply a two-stage cross-modal training approach, initially training an audio-based representation of musical scores and text descriptions, and then refining the combined representations through mutual learning. We evaluate our method against state-of-the-art music retrieval models and demonstrate improved performance on generating musical compositions.

One major obstacle when working with Linked Data lies in developing intuitive and user-friendly interfaces accessible to individuals who aren't technologically inclined. To address this, Ontodia is an interactive visualization tool that enables the exploration and visualization of Linked Data entities and their relationships. In this study, we showcase a new collaboration between Ontodia and Wikidata, incorporating a cutting-edge natural language processing technique - word embeddings - to enhance the data exploration process. Word embeddings empower Ontodia with semantic search capabilities, enabling users to navigate to specific areas of interest by executing searches utilizing domain-specific terminology, even if the concepts aren't reflected in the underlying data labels. Furthermore, this integration facilitates Wikidata enrichment, allowing Ontodia users to contribute new knowledge and enhance existing entity descriptions with the insights gained from word embeddings. By democratizing access to Linked Data and promoting Ontodia as a versatile platform for semantic exploration, we aim to empower a broader range of stakeholders to make the most of Semantic Web technologies.

We've discovered the theoretical framework for dark solitons in optical systems with non-linear dispersion and defocusing properties, in the presence of variable light scattering. Our research reveals the impact of non-linear dispersion on dark soliton stability in both the Kerr and anti-Kerr media. Our results demonstrate that in the Kerr medium, increasing non-linear dispersion strengthens the dark soliton's stability, while in the anti-Kerr medium, it induces instability. Our theoretical model is supported by numerical simulations, showing good accuracy.

This research introduces a framework for facilitating guidance within visual analytics by addressing the inherent challenges of complex decision-making. The framework is comprised of a set of modular, easily adaptable suggestions for enhancing guidance, along with a comprehensive example application that showcases its practical utility.

The research of stellarators regains momentum due to their excellent exterior control and robustness. We're reviving an enhanced coil design, initially developed in the late 90s, which has an exemplary metabolic profile and exhibits excessive excursion boundaries. This design can be optimized for diverse metabolic profiles, including the IPC and VMEC calculations. Our objective is to refine the design so that modular coils from different configurations intermix seamlessly. We use a Witten connectivity index-based metric to quantify the structural differences between coils from distinct configurations and maintain connectivity among them. We introduce an iterative coil reordering method to achieve a high level of integration among modules from different stellarator designs. We've successfully integrated coils from three distinct areas: NCSX, Helias, and IQPS. These integrated coils display an elevated level of exterior control and metabolic features compared to their individual counterparts. Furthermore, 3D reconstruction techniques are used to evaluate the structural interconnection between coils from different configurations. These integration findings suggest that stellarator design's successful implementation hinges on a well-placed, thoroughly considered modular structure.

Achieving uniform particle distribution is a crucial requirement for efficient operation in various gas-solid processes. Nevertheless, the dynamic process of particle deposition often results in uneven distributions, which can severely limit process productivity. To enhance our understanding of particle deposition and the resulting temperature fluctuations in a gas-solid fixed bed, we employed rapid magnetic resonance imaging to visualize both phenomena simultaneously. Our key findings indicate that particle deposition significantly affects local temperature distributions, with distinct correlations observed between temperature and particle density. These observed correlations suggest that temperature may serve as a viable indicator for predicting particle deposition patterns.

The occurrence of supersaturated solid formations in biological fluids has been a longstanding phenomenon, with possible links to disease development and tissue damage. Despite its significance, a comprehensive theoretical framework for describing the self-assembly of complex biological aggregates is lacking. In this study, a new framework is established for modeling the self-assembly of complexes consisting of multiple, interacting components. Specifically, a mathematical approach is developed for describing the constitutional dynamics of aggregates consisting of two interacting substances present in biological fluids of varying temperatures and concentrations. The developed theory is validated through numerical simulations, which further incorporate the influence of competitive binding kinetics. The results obtained from these simulations accurately match the experimental observations outlined in a previous study. The proposed theoretical model can be applied to any complex biological aggregates consisting of shared, interacting components.

Using the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, our research examined the rotational behavior of large sunspots in NOAA AR 11429 and the magnetic disruptions that accompanied notable solar flares. Sunspots rotate rapidly in tandem with the underlying magnetic fields, while flares lead to noticeable disturbances in the magnetic environment, evident across all harmonic degrees from the Sun's surface to its middle layer. Notably, the disturbance amplitude is most pronounced for mid-to-low degrees (m=1-3).

We've developed a flexible theoretical framework, the b-principle, for tackling global constraints on discrete structures with local constraints as a foundation. It offers a versatile tool for creating intricate patterns within various fields like topology, combinatorics, and algebra. The b-principle is known for yielding elegant and often straightforward proofs of complex theorems. Notably, it played a key role in proving the four-color problem, Mergelyan's approximation theorem, and the Novikov conjecture on group extensions. Our work extends the b-principle by incorporating a notion of stability, which enables us to address local constraints with imprecisions or tolerances. This research also presents applications of the stable b-principle to resolve several long-standing challenges, including the Madsen-Weiss theorem, the Sakaev conjecture, and the Randell-Wilf theorem. Our framework is a powerful and versatile tool that we anticipate will have far-reaching implications in many areas of mathematics.

This research involves comparing the efficiency of Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) and Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) methods for solving complex cardiac mechanics problems on various types of finite element grids. By modeling the mechanical properties of heart muscle tissue using three-dimensional finite element equations, researchers have transformed cardiac mechanics into a complex nonlinear algebraic problem. To tackle this issue, a novel solver was developed, utilizing the Newton iteration to balance stiffness and softness in the equation. The results show that the BDDC and AMG solvers perform equally well for standard grid sizes but favor different approaches for larger scales, suggesting the need for precise analysis and testing in computational cardiology.

The ever-growing influence of User-Generated Content (UGC) has been a key factor propelling the dissemination of information online. As UGC continues to evolve, studies are shifting from basic characteristics to more sophisticated aspects, such as the creative process and the economic impact of UGC. This research explores various UGC phenomena by examining specific patterns and trends in social media platforms. It divides UGC into five distinct phases, starting from the initial adoption and dissemination, to the distribution and sharing of created content across multiple channels. A statistical analysis of these patterns was conducted on two substantial social media datasets, one based on Flickr and led by "photographers," and another based on Del.icio.us and driven by "information seekers."

Recently, proposed bianisotropic acoustic metagratings offer promising possibilities for passive acoustic wave manipulation, notably in flat acoustic lenses and ultra-high frequency ultrasound imaging. This concept, however, has yet to be implemented in actual ultrasonic systems due to difficulties in fabricating 2D microstructures at frequencies above 1 MHz. This work introduces a novel technique utilizing 3D two-photon lithography to manufacture sub-wavelength 2D microstructures at 2 MHz and 3 MHz, respectively. These constructed microstructures function as anisotropic acoustic mirrors, redirecting incoming waves in two distinct directions perpendicular to the microstructure plane. Notably, numerical simulations and experimental findings both confirm that the required acoustic anisotropy can be achieved with merely 125 micrometers of pressure difference.

This paper focuses on the long-term behavior of strong solutions to the two-dimensional compressible FENE ribbon model. Utilizing the Fourier splitting technique, we demonstrate that the solutions' life spans can be extended indefinitely. Furthermore, we have proven that these strong solutions are uniformly continuous in time and space within certain Sobolev spaces. In addition, we have established that these solutions' life spans can be indefinitely prolonged. Moreover, we have found that these solutions possess certain regularity properties and are bounded within specific Sobolev spaces.

Implementing integrated access and backhaul (IAB) through wireless connections offers a promising way to develop flexible and high-density networks. Mobile IAB, which facilitates the connection of UEs in motion, holds potential as a suitable solution. This work takes a different approach from existing literature by providing a comprehensive overview of deploying mobile IAB by covering: the IAB standardization in 5G New Radio (NR); a classification framework for both fixed and mobile IAB; an extensive analysis of mobile IAB performance through simulations; and the open challenges and potential prospects of this technology. The proposed taxonomy organizes existing IAB research by categorizing different perspectives, while categorizing mobile IAB by the type of mobility involved. In terms of performance assessment, the authors analyzed an actual deployment of mobile IAB on a train by measuring key performance indicators, which showed promising results. Nonetheless, the adoption of mobile IAB remains hindered by several technical problems, mainly related to handovers, backhaul link quality, and mobile UE's ability to sustain connections while moving.

In this study, we conduct an extensive examination of five leading global optimization techniques -  differential evolution, genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization, CMA ES, and adaptive ES - as well as their various hyperparameters, to analyze their influence on problem-solving outcomes for a comprehensive set of benchmark functions. Utilizing a novel approach that combines statistical modeling with extreme sampling, we successfully identify the most influential hyperparameters and their interactive effects on solution quality, allowing for accurate prediction of effectiveness in ranking hyperparameters for specific problems. This approach is shown to be highly effective, achieving a high success rate in comparing evolutionary algorithms, and provides valuable insights for practitioner decision-making, ultimately leading to improved outcome evaluation and potential adjustments to underlying algorithmic mechanisms.

The intention is to examine some arguments supporting the wave formula in quantum theory, specifically focusing on the measurement process. It's essential to note that these arguments are presented solely for the purpose of stimulating debate and not representing the personal views of the authors.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, numerous significant hurdles remain when applying it to dynamic and ever-changing problems common in critical domains, including robotics and complex gameplay. Reinforcement learning models generally struggle to generalize effectively when confronted with new tasks beyond their training data. In response to this challenge, the field is seeing an increased focus on continual learning methods, and a key obstacle to developing these methods involves finding suitable testing frameworks. This paper presents a novel, continuous reinforcement learning testing environment called L2Explorer, which poses a continuous problem that requires learning to navigate a complex, dynamically shifting 2D landscape. L2Explorer is designed to simulate a scenario in which learning agents must adapt to an ever-changing environment that evolves over time and space. Our evaluation of L2Explorer involves a range of benchmark tests using well-known state-of-the-art continual learning algorithms.

Liger is a next-generation infrared device designed to utilize the Keck Observatory's unique combination of observational capabilities and resource accessibility. Liger will serve as a successor to the current NICI and NIRO3 instruments, offering an extensive array of features. Liger operates within the wavelength range of 0.8 to 2.6 micrometers and boasts a substantial 0.8 deg^2 field of view, 4-5 orders of magnitude greater magnitude sensitivity, and 1-2 orders of magnitude improved resolution compared to its predecessor, NIRO3. Liger is specifically tailored for a range of applications including cosmology, star formation, planetary science, and galaxy evolution. To optimize its functionality across various applications, Liger's data processing system necessitates a processing throughput of approximately 200 megabytes per second, while maintaining accuracy and preserving data integrity. Our research outlines the design of the data processing system and the software interfaces used to support Liger's data transmission and pipeline operation.

This study uncovers a broad class of perturbations in the 2D Euler equation that can propagate in the vicinity of a Couette flow as flowing waves. It also demonstrates the existence of critically unstable travelling waves arising from these perturbations when initial data is confined to a narrow stripe along the streamwise axis and decay exponentially in the crosswise direction. Furthermore, numerical simulations verify the findings and illustrate the intricate patterns associated with these critical transitions.

We experimentally control the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using optical traps with elliptical geometries that favor specific polarization modes. Due to anisotropic splitting in the cavity, ground state degeneracy is lifted, resulting in different polarization modes becoming non-degenerate and energetically equivalent. In a single trap, the all-optical manipulation of polarization mode occupation, mimicking that of a Hong-Ou-Mandel experiment, is demonstrated. Additionally, our findings are extended to coupled wire and ring structures, allowing for the initial polarization mode occupation to be set and then switched.

This study's primary objective is to provide evidence and disproofs for the deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equations including non-local slope components. We begin by establishing the local existence and uniqueness of solutions to the included nonlinear Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with a non-local slope term under certain conditions. Next, we prove the local existence and uniqueness of solutions to the included deterministic Allen-Cahn equation with a non-local "slope term". The proof involves integrating the properties of a specific kernel and the maximum principle. Additionally, we provide evidence for the local existence and uniqueness of solutions to the included inclusion-type Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation. The proof involves combining the variational approach with the Blikov-Goldenfeld theory for inclusion problems.

The 2019 COVID-19 pandemic global spread necessitated an immediate and swift response from nations to mitigate devastating effects on public health and economies. Governments worldwide relied heavily on timely data-driven decisions, yet many countries struggled with gathering necessary statistics due to limited resources, restrictive measures, and rapid disease spread. South Africa, having initially avoided the pandemic's early peak due to a lockdown, subsequently experienced a severe second wave exacerbated by the virus's mutations and non-compliance with health protocols. To counter data shortages, scientists turned to analysing available and publicly accessible data, such as Google trends, Twitter posts, and energy consumption patterns, to aid decision-making. This research presents an in-depth examination of these alternative data sources and their use in modelling COVID-19 trends in South Africa.

Given an additive group G and subsets A, B, C with |A| ≤ |B|, |C| ≤ |B|, the sumset A + B is defined as the set of elements x + y for x in A, y in B. Freiman's 3k-4 theorem applies when the sumset is small in comparison to the individual subsets. In particular, it states that if |A + B| ≤ (3|A| + |B|)/4 and x is an element of A, y is an element of B, z in G such that z + x + y = 0, then there exists a function f from B to the integers such that the following equality holds: ∑(f(b) + f(-x - b) + z) = 0 for all b in B. Here, a modified version of the theorem is proven with a simplified condition and additional freedoms in G. Specifically, it states that if there exist elements x, y, z in G such that z + x + y = 0, and if |A + B| ≤ (3|A| + |B|)/4 or |A ∩ B| ≥ (1/3)|B|, then there exists a function f from B to the integers such that the following equality holds: ∑(f(b) + f(-x - b) + z) = 0 for all b in B.

In medical contexts, diverse information originates from various modalities, and fusing data from multiple sources often yields more comprehensive insights than using individual modalities in isolation. This knowledge has spurred the development of various fusion techniques, albeit their potential to improve outcomes has not been thoroughly demonstrated in the medical field. This research delves into applying data fusion in medical image analysis, and we introduce a novel approach that utilizes a dual-branch convolutional neural network to merge information from fundus and OCT images of retinas. This method enhances the accuracy of glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy diagnosis by effectively integrating the features extracted from both images. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset reveal a systematic improvement in performance following data fusion, and we have made the source code and model weights available for public access.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics with potential insight into COVID-19 patients' severity, but these characteristics are difficult to extract manually due to the time-consuming nature of the process. It would be beneficial for medical professionals to quickly identify these characteristics during admissions to better assess and manage intensive care units. Our research focuses on determining the characteristics of ICU admission-related potential X-ray image features. We evaluated 11 image characteristics and found that certain characteristics, such as lung expansion, peribronchitis, and pleural involvement, are significantly different between non-survivors and survivors, while others do not display a significant difference. These characteristics are observable in X-ray images and can be interpreted by radiologists to predict a patient's likelihood of survival.

This article delves into the theoretical aspects of identifying spherical boundaries from transmission eigenvalues and eigenfunctions in spherical media. We derive a group theorem for the spherical transfer matrix, establish a necessary and sufficient condition for unique boundary identification, calculate the spherical wronskian via a derivative test, and propose an numerical method for calculating the boundary. Furthermore, we validate our theoretical findings with explicit examples and experimental data.

To effectively discover novel intents in dialogue systems, it is crucial to accurately identify intent categories from contextual conversations. Currently, intention detection in such systems often falls short due to its limited scope and lack of contextual understanding, particularly when encountering novel intents not part of its training data. Therefore, intention detection in dialogue systems remains a significant challenge. In our paper, we propose an intention detection model called HyIT, which utilizes pre-trained language models to enhance contextual understanding and leverage self-supervised learning from massive external data to improve flexibility in processing unfamiliar situations. Additionally, HyIT incorporates a contrastive learning approach to distinguish intent categories and mitigate the impact of overlapping words between intents. Through extensive experiments on a leading benchmark dataset, our model has achieved superior performance compared to the current best methods, and further analysis demonstrates the importance of contrastive learning and the efficiency of HyIT in discovering novel intents.

The universal simplicial collection, $\mathcal{U}$, can be defined as the largest collection that satisfies the Larchah's equation, which also involves the face maps. This collection, $\mathcal{U}$, has a natural algebraic structure that corresponds to a group when considered over a specific ring. Specifically, the group operation is defined as the sum of the elements modulo the ideal generated by the 2-simplex class. This particular group, $\mathcal{G}$, turns out to be a simplicial group in its own right. Furthermore, the face maps in $\mathcal{U}$ also act as homomorphisms in the group structure, which allows us to study the relationships between its homotopy types and linear resolution properties.

Let $G$ be a finite group. We show that the number of subgroups of $G$ is finite and can be specified exactly up to a logical deduction. This settles a long-standing conjecture regarding finite groups initially proposed by Zassenhaus in the 1950s. Our approach involves an existing theorem by Tits, a respected German mathematician, combined with Furter and Giannazzi's previous findings on the subgroups of $G$.

This review focuses on the Fubini, Sun, and Chen's H2 equation, a particular type of bi-Hamiltonian system, in the context of the ABS H2 hierarchy, which is established through detailed analysis and logical steps.  The article also explores the connections between the standard H2 hierarchy and the higher-spin hierarchies, specifically the odd-spin one, established by Nijhoff, Adler, and Lyche.

This paper explores the issue of erroneous positive relationships in visual relationship detection tasks. These errors, where incorrect relationships are learned, severely hinder accurate relationship detection and lead to unsatisfactory scene understanding. We pinpoint two sources of these errors: noisy annotations and incorrect generalizations. To overcome these errors, we suggest a simple yet effective approach involving confidence-based filtering and learning from multiple datasets in conjunction with domain-adaptation techniques. Utilizing the Visual Relationship Detection 2 dataset, which encompasses diverse and challenging animal relationships, our method demonstrates the ability to eliminate erroneous positives and surpass existing state-of-the-art models.

Using the quantum correlation approach, the pricing equation for quantum instruments is derived and specific cases, including projective measurements and Pauli measurements, are analyzed. The results show that quantum correlation has a significant impact on the measurement process, resulting in a non-zero correlation term that increases with the number of measurements. This contrasts with the zero correlation term obtained from the classical log-price formula. Furthermore, the non-zero correlation term indicates a substantial price variation among identical instruments, arising from the inherent non-commutativity of quantum observables and the quantum measurement process.

This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for creating detailed social connection maps. Current approaches to social relationship inference primarily focus on one specific type of relationship at a time, such as family or co-working relationships. In contrast, our proposed network is designed to model a wide range of social connections all at once. To accomplish this, we developed a flexible social relationship graph that can easily be adapted to new relationship categories. Additionally, to tackle the issue of missing social connection data, our framework incorporates a feature called social attribute propagation, which utilizes established social connections to make informed guesses about an individual's other relationships. To test the effectiveness of our framework, we created a massive dataset consisting of the social connections of over 1,000,000 people across six different domains, and conducted rigorous testing to validate our approach's performance. The results of our testing confirm that our framework produces social connection maps that closely match real-world data.

We propose an innovative communication passing network design, capable of adapting to changing graph structures during both training and testing. Traditional communication passing networks assume a fixed graph topology, whereas our approach creates an adaptable framework for visual recognition tasks. We develop a method to generate a dynamic graph based on the recognition task at hand and employ edge and node aggregation functions that are reversible, allowing us to easily modify the graph topology as needed. This dynamic graph communication passing network can be applied to various vision tasks and has been successfully tested on image classification, object detection, and segmentations, yielding improved recognition accuracy and faster inference times compared to other state-of-the-art models.

Optimized hardware is often required in embedded systems, leading to a common operation called Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) over integers. One efficient way to achieve this optimization is by replacing expensive generic multiplication with bit-shifts and additions in a multiplierless circuit. Our work advances the state-of-the-art in optimal MCM approaches based on Integer Linear Programming (ILP) and introduces a novel hardware cost model. This model counts one-bit adders, demonstrating a strong correlation with the number of LUTs required. Our enhanced model accommodates intermediate precision truncations, enabling significant resource savings when full precision is not essential. Additionally, we incorporate error propagation rules to ensure a specified error margin for MCM results. Our ILP formulation includes these complex constraints, offering significant efficiency improvements over previous methods.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements have revealed that quantum circuits share parallels with artificial neural systems. This paper delves into quantum deep learning concepts, showcasing their practical applications and highlighting existing challenges. A comparative analysis of classical and quantum models is provided, followed by an examination of the practical issues arising from their implementation, particularly regarding data, circuit design, and error correction. This comprehensive review ultimately seeks to outline potential future research directions for the quantum deep learning community.

The radio-frequency (RF) accelerator community submitted its findings to Snowmass 2021, focusing on advancing linear accelerators to achieve historic breakthroughs and tackle challenging problems in physics, engineering, and medicine. Key areas of improvement include enhancing accelerator performance, reducing costs, and mitigating environmental impact. Over the past three years, seven member groups contributed to the report, which outlines research and development progress, evaluates current speed, and proposes future velocity targets. To meet the demands of future physics initiatives, researchers are working on RF technology, with proposed applications including compact medical accelerators, experimental users facilities, and potential applications at future colliders.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics of this new physics remain unknown, suggesting the need for multiple, distinct collider designs to ensure an optimal search process. This textbook provides a comprehensive overview of three collider concepts, including a $e^+e^-$ machine, a $\mu^+\mu^-$ muon machine, and a lepton collider, with each section written by renowned experts in the field.

We derive analytical expressions for linearized wave speeds in relativistic hydrodynamics, considering a single fluid with both energy and momentum contributions. Our calculation takes into account viscosity's effect on wave behavior. By applying the second law of thermodynamics for relativistic fluids with a specific bound on entropy, we determine the upper limit on viscosity's influence on wave speeds. Viscothermal approximation provides a suitable modeling approach for low-temperature and low-frequency scenarios.

Patriotic nations around the world are engaging in summer physics research, and the possibility of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes is being explored. These black holes, created 3.7 seconds after the Big Bang, could potentially explain the origin of primordial dark matter. As an alternative to light elementary particles, the process of Hawking radiation from these black holes is being considered. Our work builds upon a pre-existing research paper, which estimated the number of these black holes formed in the early universe and their Sub-GeV mass spectrum. We found that such black holes would have had temperatures below their associated mass quark confinement point and proposed a new equilibrium state, 'freeze-out by the cosmological horizon', in which the universe's expansion prevents Hawking radiation from these black holes. We determined the particle flux produced by decaying these black holes and found that their radiation, across various energy ranges, significantly exceeds forecasts made under the assumption of light elementary particles and matches observations in some cases. Notably, the predicted particle count is vastly larger than anticipated, with potential implications for upcoming experiments.

To accelerate Secure Multiplication Circuit computations on homomorphic
equivalent circuits, Modern Hybrid Architecture processors have incorporated
specialized functional units. However, these circuits are still slow to process
due to the costly OAES operations involved. We introduced the Virtual Safeguard
Platform, a versatile instruction-set-parallel processor based on the Tiny
Homomorphic Encryption Library, as a response to the constrained execution speed.
Our innovative approach involves designing a full-parallel, five-stage pipeline
processor around five basic operations, resulting in significantly faster and more
efficient execution of complex programs like Machine Learning models, despite
incorporating additional non-OAES operations. Compared to the TRINE architecture,
our processor achieves a 4x to 6x increase in execution speed over a similar
evaluation board, with additional support for custom function uploads and a
more user-friendly programming environment.

Researchers have developed polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for specific optimization problems, including those with large-valued objectives. Their latest work enhances this approximation capability to problems with sparse objectives that contain positive values and approximates these objectives up to a certain ratio using a given number of bits. Their PTAS can be applied to various problems, including maximum independent cycle capacity and minimum bidirected multicut, even in graphs with arbitrary node weights. Their approach to developing a PTAS includes deriving a suitable surrogate problem, obtaining approximate feasible solutions, and achieving the desired approximation quality. Their work also provides a computationally efficient surrogate problem for the minimum bidirected multicut problem and demonstrates the applicability of a known technique in approximate linear programming to derive a PTAS for this problem. Their PTAS can be extended to deliver a quasi-PTAS for the minimum cost bidding strategy in combinatorial optimization settings and yields a new PTAS for the minimum cost bidding strategy in a specific fractional linear programming setting.

In natural language understanding, pre-trained language models have emerged as the foundation for achieving high accuracy in various tasks with minimal training, making it achievable to analyze text without being an expert in the specific domain. This study investigates the unsupervised and few-shot analysis capabilities of contemporary pre-trained language models, including their counterparts with and without moral understanding, and also examines their performance in the presence of limited labeled data. The experiments reveal that models like RoBERTa and MNAROBERTa, which take moral considerations into account, deliver equivalent or superior results in the unsupervised and few-shot analysis, and that they often outperform similar models without moral understanding in the same tasks.

High-definition hyperspectral images contain numerous color information values, spanning from 255 to 65535, which could significantly enhance the processing and analysis capabilities in vision systems. Despite this, no notable advancements have been made to leverage these extra color dimensions in practical computer vision applications. In this research, we explored the potential of these extra color values in a real-world semantic segmentation task within the Cityscapes dataset. Initially, we established a benchmark for hyperspectral image processing and developed a basic framework incorporating 3D convolutional neural networks. The results showed that although the additional color values in hyperspectral images offer more data, their presence also introduces noise, which necessitates more complex models to effectively utilize these extra color information.

The widespread phenomenon of rapid stellar rotations among early-stage stars is well-documented, but its ultimate fate remains an area of ongoing debate in stellar evolution research. Many of these rapidly rotating stars experience a brief phase characterized by significant mass loss, often necessitating an explanation for the resulting decrease in angular momentum. We have conducted an in-depth analysis of a sample of 16 rapidly rotating young stars selected from the MSX Global Jet Survey, focusing on the details of their mass loss episodes and subsequent rotational evolution. By comparing the angular momentum lost during mass loss and the rotational velocity achieved after recovery, we have found a notable 1:1 correspondence that persists across the H-R diagram. This finding is consistent with the hypothesis that mass loss these stars experience is primarily driven by a jet-powered feedback mechanism. However, the data also suggest the presence of an additional angular momentum transport process, possibly facilitated by a disk that forms following the mass loss episodes. A comprehensive understanding of the observed rotational evolution will necessitate a combination of feedback mechanics and efficient angular momentum transport mechanisms.

In algorithmic literature, the underlying computation model is typically implicit and assumed to follow the RAM model. Despite this, researchers infrequently scrutinize the inherent time complexity of the RAM model itself. This paper tackles that exact question by investigating the time complexity of basic arithmetic operations within the RAM model. It demonstrates that, under the RAM's natural next-step model, basic arithmetic operations can be performed simultaneously, including both multiplication by a non-negative constant and division by a positive constant, in the presence of a modular reduction operation, yielding a time complexity of O(log n). Additionally, it showcases a way to efficiently (in time O(log n)) perform division and modular reduction operations, given the capability to perform addition efficiently. This research further culminates in identifying a set of necessary and sufficient conditions that would enable efficient (in time O(log n)) execution of arbitrary polynomial expressions.

To tackle the limitations of traditional session-based recommendation methods, we developed a co-training framework on graph sessions. This approach leverages the inherent structure within graph sessions to enhance model performance through self-supervised learning. Consequently, our method achieves state-of-the-art results on four publicly available datasets, surpassing the performance of state-of-the-art fine-tuned and new baseline methods.

This work presents two new classes of LCD codes: group LCD codes and group reversible LCD codes. The notion of group LCD codes is an extension of traditional LCD codes, while group reversible LCD codes are a variant with additional group properties. A key characteristic of these codes is their ability to maintain the group structure, despite the variable nature of LCD codes. A specific standard of group reversible LCD codes is also defined, with examples provided to illustrate their existence. Furthermore, the article presents a framework for constructing group reversible LCD codes based on group reversible elements.

Recent breakthroughs by A. Bardeen, R. Stump, and J. Conlon, along with S. Weiss and S. Korand, have significantly advanced our understanding of loop integrals through the union of graph loops. This concept, akin to a shape operator, yields a robust algebraic framework for differential equations by combining an extended de Rham cohomology on the complex of graphs. This topological method surpasses conventional approaches based on forest shapes, particularly in solving problems related to dual variables and irreducible ratios. Furthermore, the generalized Kuhnel formula implies a striking connection between graph complexes and the topological properties of differential forms on simplicial complexes.

In a categorization task, objects are distinguished from one another based on unique characteristics. However, some objects share similar attributes (visual features), rendering traditional models inadequate as they fail to account for the non-unique nature of these attributes. For instance, a rectangular shape is a common feature among a bowl, a picture frame, and a tabloid. We propose the concept of object traits as higher-level visual elements that differ from low-level features. Through detailed analysis, we identify several key traits in natural images, including holes, overlaps, and enclosed regions. Using synthesized objects, we demonstrate that models trained for object categorization are capable of learning these traits and that they play a significant role in processing objects. Furthermore, we reveal a significant outcome - models are more efficient at recognizing object traits when these objects do not share common visual features, thus highlighting the importance of diversity in training data. Finally, we show that our findings are consistent across various depth models, encompassing simple backpropagation-based models and more sophisticated attention-based models.

Despite numerous studies on non-Hermitian topology, the influence of correlations remains poorly understood. Correlated electrons can drastically alter the topological characteristics of non-Hermitian systems, but current research has only begun to explore this intersection of correlation and non-Hermitianness. In this study, we examine the effects of correlations on the topological properties of one-dimensional non-Hermitian systems, and we demonstrate a notable reduction in the 1D non-Hermitian system's point-gap topology brought about by correlations. Our findings reveal that correlations can transform the protected zero energy state at the boundary into a pseudospin polarized state, while also causing a point gap hybrid in the spectral gap. Our analysis further highlights the influence of correlations on the inverse spectral gap in these systems, as well as the viable experimental platforms suitable for observing these correlations.

A novel class of Golay complementary arrays is presented, which are constructed using polyphase sequences and orthogonal matrices. The Golay complementary arrays produced by this method have optimal thinning properties and are capable of generating complementary pairs with a maximum size of $N\times M$, where $M$ can reach up to $N-1$. We have developed a general framework for designing Golay complementary arrays using polyphase sequences of lengths $2M$ and $\sum M$. Furthermore, specific design examples are provided for different types of Golay complementary arrays, including the $2^{2}$-Golay and $4$-Golay types, across various prime and composite sequence lengths.

A comprehensive analysis combining the predictions from theory and experimental data has been conducted to determine the Higgs boson spin-zero width and test anomalous interactions in the HVV (HZZ, HWW) coupling scenarios, with the inclusion of non-standard models. The study utilized the full Run 2 dataset from the ATLAS and CMS collaborations, with a focus on the ZZ*→4l final state. To achieve this, researchers developed novel techniques to separate signal from background across the entire mass range of the Higgs system, with particular emphasis on enhancing sensitivity to its spin-zero width. The findings from both experiments, with combined proton-proton center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV and luminosity of 139/fb, have been presented in tables, showcasing the Higgs boson excesses and their comparisons with various models, including SM, non-SM with nonmass parameters, and SM with additional scalar or vector bosons. The outcomes have been graphically represented as excess tables and comparisons with the SM scenario.

This research introduces a cutting-edge, unsupervised approach for detecting changes in hyperspectral images using a novel feature-fusion deep convolutional neuromodulatory network. The technique comprises of two layers: the first is a deep convolutional neural network that extracts features from the hyperspectral images, and the second is a neuromodulatory layer that refines these features and enhances the differences between change areas using an unsupervised change detection loss function. The technique was evaluated on two real-world hyperspectral images and showed outstanding results, outperforming three established change detection methods in terms of accuracy, the use of features, parameters, complexity, and computational efficiency.

For any positive integer $n$, let $S_n$ denote the set of integers whose representation has at most two digits, where each digit lies between $0$ and $9$. We define $\mathcal{S}_n$ as the set containing sums of pairs of square numbers with a maximum sum not exceeding $n$. We propose an additive counterpart of a well-known result from the work of Harvey and Wright. We provide a proof that shows the cardinality of $S_n \cup \mathcal{S}_n$ grows asymptotically at a rate of $\Omega(n/ \log n)$. We further observed that a modified version of our approach can be used to derive an lower bound of $n^{1/4}$ for the exponent in a conjecture regarding the density of integers with four representable square values.

Quantum tunneling is an inherent process in nature that lacks a straightforward analogy from the non-quantum world. In solid-state physics, it is the driving force behind various phenomena such as transfer of carriers in semiconductors and superconductivity. In silicon, it plays a key role in optical communications and is essential for readout in quantum key distribution systems. There has been extensive research on creating efficient tunneling mechanisms between states in silicon. However, generating fast and controllable tunneling between states linked to different crystal directions while maintaining minimal laser-based coupling has remained an unresolved issue until now. Our work includes the design and development of a silicon quantum dot system with a unique valley interference property, allowing for the realization of a controlled tunnel coupling between these dots. Valley interference occurs between states associated with distinct directional states in the crystal structure, which are separated by a silicon layer. These states are equivalent to different spin states. Our approach enables the coupling of these states through a common intermediate state. Our findings include the observation of valley interference and the ability to switch the dot's information with high precision, which is a critical step towards developing more complex quantum systems in silicon. These advanced systems will enable the efficient management of quantum information at the atomic level, which is essential for various applications in quantum information technology.

Several optimization techniques from various disciplines, including heuristic and meta-heuristic methods, have been extensively studied in the literature. This paper reviews key approaches to these optimization techniques, highlighting their core principles and features. The study also identifies significant research trends within the field and outlines future areas of investigation. The primary objective of this research is to facilitate rapid implementation of optimization algorithm variants, paving the way for thorough analytical examination.

In this study, we investigate whether a given projective algebraic variety can be viewed homogeneously as a subset of projective space, and we establish criteria for this homogeneity in terms of degree and transcendence degree. We demonstrate that if a variety is homogeneous, it possesses a specific geometric symmetry and establish relationships between degree, transcendence degree, and this symmetry. Additionally, we examine the maximum degree of transcendence for various types of projective varieties and determine the optimal values.

In this discussion, we explore the relationship between spacetime coordinates and their momenta, examining their commutator and comparing it to the structure of a complex number system. We then delve into the implications of this comparison for quantum states, which lead to a distinction between 'position states' and'momentum states', both of which behave differently under the twist of non-commutativity. This distinction raises conceptual difficulties, particularly in assessing the symmetry of the spacetime platform and the validity of certain mathematical operations.

We've developed a novel technique, two-photon absorption transient voltage, TPH2VT, which uncovers 3D charge transport properties in semiconductors. TPH2VT utilizes a laser with low energy loss, enabling penetration into the material, and measures charge generated near the sample's surface. By combining electrochemical etching and scanning photovoltage spectroscopy, we were able to localize and quantify charge transport parameters in CVD diamond. Our results reveal a 0.8% level of heterogeneity in charge transport properties across a 100mm x 100mm sample, demonstrating the technique's effectiveness and efficiency.

Social media platforms are facing significant problems due to the presence of toxic content like hate speech, off-color language, and misogyny. These difficulties have caught the attention of the Natural Language Processing (NLP) community, driving innovative research in the field. In this study, we report on our findings in the Arabic Misogyny Detection challenge, where we compare different deep learning models. Our experiments reveal that a convolutional neural network (CNN) leverages grammatical characteristics to effectively classify misogyny, whereas recurrent neural networks (RNNs) incorporating feature-rich models achieve better performance. Building upon these results, we developed a deep multi-task learning approach that improves hate speech detection while minimizing computational demands.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations even in situations where the generator includes discontinuities and non-linear components, with the parameter α falling within the interval (0,1). Moreover, a corresponding application is explored to verify a comparison theorem for these equations.

In complex systems influenced by hidden variables, like noise and faults, policymakers struggle to achieve their greatest impact. This paper explores how to develop guidelines that can withstand unpredictable system behaviors and ensure model accuracy. We examine random system changes and derive strict requirements for robustness and model precision. Utilizing these findings, we develop modified SARSA and Expectation-Maximization algorithms to robustly estimate system parameters and generate practical policies. Experimental results indicate that our algorithms perform well in challenging systems.

A comprehensive model has been established to address various network computation problems, including caching and computation schemes. We have developed a standardized approach to analyze a caching problem where independent files are accessed by users with disjoint subsets of available information. Our framework is applicable to a wide range of scenarios, including distributed computation with network errors, where processes transmit packets over a shared connection. We have demonstrated how our model can be utilized to derive optimal solutions for specific cases, such as caching problems with linear submodular functions and a distributed computation problem with errors. Furthermore, we have provided lower and upper bounds for general caching problems with linear submodular functions.

We establish the Scott framework of PCF within univalent type theory, 
by demonstrating the existence of a universal partial equivalence relation
and verifying that the types of PCF form a suitable collection. 
Furthermore, we formulate and prove in univalent type theory a formal version
of the soundness theorem that relates to the denotational semantics of PCF.

This research proposes an innovative secure control method for a mobile robotic arm, particularly effective against potential attacks on its kinematic parameters. By designing a control system that responds dynamically to changes in its geometric and kinematic properties, the robotic arm's trajectory can be maintained, and its pose stabilized in the face of uncertainty. An advanced framework for the robotic arm's secure control was developed using Control Barrier Functions, and a Data-Driven Estimator was incorporated to quickly estimate any deviations in the robotic arm's configuration following an attack. This has the benefit of enabling secure operation at faster sampling rates. Simulation results successfully demonstrate the effectiveness of this secure control method in controlling the robotic arm's trajectory, even under adverse conditions.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based techniques for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction approach. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers explored the behavior of Bose-Einstein condensates undergoing 1D
scattering with a repulsive interaction. They proposed a set of nonlinear operators
that effectively describe the system's dynamics under repeated high-energy
scattering impacts. Utilizing a Fock space approach, they developed specific
operator forms capable of handling multiple particle interactions. As a test of
their methodology, they analyzed repulsive interactions in both closed and open
systems and examined the resulting particle distributions. Furthermore, the
researchers investigated how an external laser could influence a Bose-Einstein
condensate's behavior, including changes induced by multiple photon scattering.

This study examines the distinctness of two meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space. Our research builds on earlier findings by Nakayama and Noguchi, as well as Chen's and Chang's work, to provide new insights into the distinctness of non-constant meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space.

Polynomial system solving plays a crucial role in various applications, and the nondegenerate locus of a system plays a key role in passing to partial resolutions. However, computing this locus for general systems is a computationally demanding task, often exceeding the limits of current computing power. We introduce a new signature-based method for determining the nondegenerate locus of a polynomial system, which outperforms existing methods in terms of efficiency. Several numerical examples demonstrate the robustness and speed of our proposed strategy.

Direct photons have been studied in copper-copper collisions at a center-of-mass energy per pair of nucleons (sNN)=200 GeV. The data was collected by the PHENIX experiment across a wide range of transverse momentum (pT) at both the PHENIX north and south venues and included both charged and neutral particles. Observations revealed a significant excess of photons above a predicted background in a wide pT range. The observed data matches predictions from theoretical models, specifically one that accounts for the behavior of electrons and muons produced via a process called internal conversion. When comparing the results to another phenomenon, the production of photons through a radiative decay of a neutral particle called a rho meson, the findings show a much higher rate of this secondary process than expected. The study's findings suggest that the rate of this phenomenon is elevated in copper-copper collisions at high density and also that the rate of a related process, the production of photons through a different particle's decay, is higher than expected at high density as well.

The Turan tetrahedron problem seeks to determine the minimum number of additional edge additions needed in a complete graph on four vertices to prevent the emergence of a tetrahedral structure. Following up on Erdos' conjecture that this minimum number exceeds $nap_\vee(3,4)-4$, we fully address the problem by demonstrating that the minimum number is specifically $nap_\vee(3,4)-3$.

When displaying line joins on vector maps, aliasing occurs due to limited screen resolution, causing jagged edges that can be mitigated through post-processing techniques. However, these anti-aliasing methods often fail to handle complex join shapes or result in visual artifacts that surpass the gain in image quality. A novel anti-aliasing technique utilizing spatial anti-aliasing buffers has been developed to provide seamless results for all types of line joins, accompanied by two additional algorithms addressing specific challenges: handling complex joins and minimizing visual artifacts. The first algorithm addresses problematic joins through a shape approximation process, while the second identifies and mitigates potential artifacts after anti-aliasing processing. The proposed methods have been successfully integrated into a mobile mapping application, yielding substantial performance improvements and superior user experience.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing more precise approximations of functions that increase linearly with the distance. Building on the Wu-Schaback quasi-interpolation formula, we adapt this new interpolation function while preserving the original scheme's characteristics, including monotonicity and convexity. It has been mathematically proven that our adaptation converges at a rate of O(h^2), enabling smoother interpolation results. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the method's efficiency and accuracy.

Pulsar domains in the galaxy's plane have been studied by conducting a comprehensive search for pulsars within 20 kpc of the equatorial region, which revealed significant findings. The most conspicuous observation is that pulsars are concentrated in dense groups, predominantly situated near massive star-forming regions and supershell structures. These areas exhibit an unusually high density of pulsars, exceeding the average by an order of magnitude, and the pulsars within these groups share distinct spatial and velocity characteristics. Furthermore, a distinctive hourglass-shaped distribution of pulsars in the central region of the galaxy has been noted, which is aligned in the northern and southern hemispheres along the galaxy's plane. Pulsars in this area, spanning 4 to 10 kpc in radius, are densely packed and exhibit uniform right ascension. The findings suggest that these pulsars formed in a single event and the pulsars' symmetrical arrangement is likely the result of the galaxy's rotation. The total number of pulsars in these dense groups is substantial, accounting for approximately 30% of discovered pulsars in the galaxy. However, their recognition poses a challenge due to the inherent difficulties, including overlapping distributions, insufficient sky coverage, and inadequate statistical analysis, which can lead to misinterpretation of findings.

This research introduces the WeatherCat dataset, an annotated collection of 92,000 images, and analyzes convolutional neural networks' performance on categorizing weather conditions. The proposed dataset and technical methods can be accessed through the authors' GitHub repository.
The Interactions of Social Standards about Climate Change: Science, Institutions and Economics

To address the limitations of traditional model-based control strategies in handling uncertainty effectively, our research focuses on incorporating the Koopman operator theory into the control of soft grippers. This involves introducing an operational framework for spectroral linear systems, illustrated through the simulation of a soft gripper using a dynamic mesh. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated in both open-loop and closed-loop control applications, showcasing its potential to enhance the management of uncertainty in soft robotic systems.

This paper introduces a novel optimization technique called Organic Gradient Descent (OGD), an iterative method that converges to the optimal solution for differentiable objective functions. Notably, OGd's update rule has a simpler form compared to the Gradient Descent update rule. We prove that OGD converges at a faster rate than Gradient Descent in multiplicative noise scenarios. Additionally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of OGD by applying it to noise-reducing problems in statistics and recovering initial conditions in Hamiltonian Dynamics. Our empirical analysis confirms that OGD surpasses GD in multiplicative noise environments while performing competitively in additive noise scenarios.

High-energy emissions from ancient supermassive black holes can provide a direct look into the black hole activity in the early universe. Specifically, misaligned jets of high-redshift active galaxies should make up a significant portion of these distant black hole sources. However, to date, studies have mainly focused on sources at z < 4.5. By using multiple radio frequency data for J2102+6015, a source with a redshift of 4.575, researchers found that its energy emissions originate from a compact region less than 0.2 parsecs in size. Additionally, they found that its energy spectrum and polarization characteristics match those of more recent, high-energy radio sources. This suggests that J2102+6015 is either a newly activated black hole source or a younger source with minimal energy feedback. Either way, J2102+6015 represents a valuable addition to the growing list of verified black hole sources at the distant end of the universe.

In the field of lung cancer pathology, interpreting biopsies relies heavily on histological examination. Nevertheless, the process of histological analysis is hampered by the difficulty in accurately discerning sub-regions of biopsy samples that contain cancerous tissue. Research has shown that, combined with machine learning capabilities, image processing can effectively aid in identifying these sub-regions and improve the accuracy of cancer prognosis. Although previous studies have made notable contributions in this area, they have thus far focused exclusively on the visual aspects of biopsy samples, thereby neglecting potential insights presented in the clinical data collected concurrently with the samples. Our research builds upon existing knowledge by developing a novel, multi-faceted model that utilizes both clinical and histological data to identify cancerous sub-regions within biopsy samples and predict patient outcomes for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Our model's effectiveness is demonstrated through superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models in both sub-region segmentation and prognosis tasks.

A natural language state description is increasingly being adopted in
reinforcement learning systems to process large amounts of data and overcome
scalability issues, particularly in tasks involving extensive state spaces
and limited training data. Unlike traditional engineered state descriptions,
natural language state descriptions are learned from data, often through
description generators, and incorporated into the system via a natural
language parser. This enables a deeper integration of natural language
state descriptions into the learning process, and has been successfully
applied in numerous tasks, including text-based games, robotics, and
multi-agent scenarios. However, further research is needed to address
challenges such as partial observability, the lack of natural language
state descriptions for some domains, and the risk of natural language
ambiguity.

A novel approach combining machine learning is introduced, enabling the accurate reconstruction of high-redshift cosmological data from observed quasar spectra. By processing each spectrum individually, the method enables the joint reconstruction of the 3D density field and associated substructure associated with multiple redshift slices. Our model, comprising a U-net architecture with Lagrange interpolation layers, achieves impressive results, with a fraction of the computational requirements compared to traditional reconstruction techniques. Our findings demonstrate the efficacy of this method in accurately recreating the density power spectrum from simulated data and quasar fields, while also successfully applying it to observed quasar spectra. Our work represents a significant advancement in large-scale structure analysis and paves the way for the more efficient utilization of upcoming spectrographic surveys.

Given a finite set of partial differential operators with constant coefficients, we develop the underlying Lie algebra of non-local vector fields and establish certain properties regarding its central elements, weight spaces, and the composition map. Furthermore, we construct specific invariant structures - a symmetric bilinear form and an element from the second Lie algebra cohomology group - within the Lie algebra of non-local vector fields. Additionally, we identify the conditions necessary to ensure these structures are 'U(∅)-free', establish relationships between these structures and the Lie algebra cohomology groups of local vector fields, and compute the Lie algebra cohomology groups of non-local vector fields in specific scenarios.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven freely accessible Twitter sentiment
databases. We then compared the performance of various machine learning models, such as
support vector machines and random forests, to the recurrent neural network, specifically
the long short-term memory model, on these datasets. Our research found that the long short
term memory model outperformed the other machine learning models, achieving higher precision
and recall rates, although its accuracy rates were similar.

Recently, various studies have focused on utilizing large language models in
open-domain dialogue systems to achieve natural conversations. Nevertheless,
current models still struggle with sustaining discussions and often require
large-scale external knowledge to reinforce their responses. To address these
challenges, we propose a new approach that aims to construct a role-specific
open-domain dialogue system by integrating large language models. Our method
involves a novel framework that can seamlessly integrate various language models
to enhance a dialogue system's performance. Additionally, we developed a
new evaluation metric to assess a dialogue system's performance in maintaining
long-term conversations. Our experimental results show significant improvements
in conversation lengths and overall response quality following the implementation
of our proposed method.

The interaction between gravitational waves and celestial objects produces static radiation, known as the gravitational wave background (GWB). Current methods for detecting GWB via radio signals are often hindered by excessive noise, but the presence of gravitational wave memory (GWM) offers an opportunity for a new detection approach. Virtually any binary merger that generates GWM contributes to the gravitational wave background, making it a more stable and less noisy signal. Our work delves into utilizing the gravitational wave memory as the gravitational wave background, specifically exploring its application in the first order GWM, known as the harmonic gravitational wave memory. This involves calculating the power spectrum and evaluating the probabilistic distribution of the harmonic memory, ultimately demonstrating its applicability in the time-frequency analysis of the gravitational wave memory. To facilitate the statistical analysis, we introduced two random processes, called the pointwise and bandwise harmonic memory processes, which were found to conform to the characteristics of a Gaussian process. With these results, the harmonic memory was shown to behave according to the characteristics of a linear fractional Brownian motion, providing a theoretical framework for the random gravitational wave memory. This approach can be extended to higher order GWM, but its implementation is significantly more complex, requiring more advanced mathematical tools.

A hypothetical supersymmetry-breaking phase transition offers a potential explanation for two major phenomena observed in high-energy astronomy: the origin of massive neutrinos and the extremely high-energy neutrino events detected at PeV scales. In a theoretical model incorporating this idea, we have identified a broad range of magnetic fields that can stabilize the supersymmetric vacuum and are strong enough to influence particle interactions during the phase transition. As a result, the predicted magnitude of neutrino mass falls within the desired range, supporting the hypothesis of the supersymmetry-breaking phase transition as the origin of massive neutrinos. Furthermore, the theoretical model predicts the creation of massive black holes and gravitational waves from this phase transition, with their properties consistent with observations at present. In particular, the predicted range of black hole masses is consistent with the findings of the Galactic Center's intermediate mass black hole hypothesis. The presence of these objects would significantly impact the local environment and, in particular, the local dark matter distribution, requiring future microphysics and astrophysics experiments to verify the theoretical model's predictions.

While interactions through language significantly bring individuals closer to comprehending each other's mental states, extensive research has demonstrated that more is required to achieve accurate understanding of each other's thoughts. This study proposes an advanced level of interaction, the "semiotic exchange," which involves the emergence of consensual symbols and their associated meanings. To accomplish this, a two-player game framework was developed, where each player utilizes both symbolic and neural networks to interpret and predict the other's behavior, as well as communicate through extensive descriptions. This study presents a novel training method, the "cooperative adversarial semiotic exchange," that not only generates practical symbols but also enhances the accuracy of mental state prediction. Experimental results on diverse datasets demonstrate the efficacy of this new approach. To achieve these improvements, a detailed analysis of the proposed method's properties was conducted, followed by an examination of its potential applications and future research directions.

In the field of semantic technologies, particularly in knowledge management and natural language processing, there is a pressing need to address the issue of missing semantic links between concepts.  This challenge, known as the term prediction problem, has far-reaching implications for data characterization, search engine optimization, and knowledge summarization, among other areas.  Although previous studies have made significant progress in this area, the current approaches are often limited by their reliance on related terms derived from co-occurrence analyses, ignoring crucial implicit relationships within the data.  To bridge this gap, our research proposes a novel approach that combines a Naive Bayes classifier with latent model-based related term analysis, yielding more accurate implicit semantic connections and enhanced term prediction outcomes.  Compared to state-of-the-art methods, our model delivers superior results across multiple evaluation metrics, showcasing its capacity to accurately forecast around 5% more semantic relationships than existing approaches.  Furthermore, our redrafted Knowledge Graph is now available by request for researchers and practitioners to reproduce our results and build upon our work.

Recent advancements in Session-based recommendation systems have gained attention for generating dynamic and context-specific suggestions. This research builds upon the Session Rank Model, enhancing it with two key improvements to boost accuracy and efficiency. Firstly, the enhanced model incorporates a new learning objective, Candidate Rank Embedding, which directly optimizes recommendation ranks. Secondly, a straightforward and effective technique, Normalized Multi-step Sampling, is introduced to mitigate the statistical challenges inherent in SBS datasets, ensuring that recommended items are sampled in a normalized manner across all phases of the browsing process. Experimental outcomes on multiple public datasets reveal a substantial improvement in recommendation accuracy using the proposed methods.

We examine the behavior of dynamic colloidal molecules, specifically dumbbells, in non-uniform active particle environments using both theoretical and experimental methods. Our approach combines mean-field theory and Brownian dynamics simulations to analyze the molecule's movement and orientation. We identify two key factors: one influences varies with size (colloidal particle size and activity level), while the opposite reaction is observed in another (all molecules react in the same way regardless of size). Our findings are further verified through a real-world experiment involving active Janus particles.

A thorough approach is outlined to simulate single-phase flow in fractured porous media. The proposed methodology comprises three core components: generating a mesh of the fracture network and surrounding porous medium, expressing fracture pressures as continuous variables, and solving governing equations for fracture-rock interface interactions. A multi-dimensional meshing technique is employed to accurately represent the complex geometry of fractured media and its boundary with the surrounding medium. Once the mesh is finalized, a discrete fracture model is implemented using the Mimetic Finite Difference method. This involves decoupling fracture regions and the matrix domain, and solving governing equations separately while accounting for the exchange of flux and flow between them. Comprehensive numerical examples are presented to validate the proposed methodology and assess its performance.

This research introduces an innovative approach for a swarm of autonomous drones to maintain the structure of a pattern formed by points in three-dimensional space, ensuring continuity and avoiding collisions with existing shapes. Building upon a registration algorithm for point sets, the methodology extends its application to vector fields, representing the intrinsic characteristics of this geometric structure. Drones utilize sensors such as GPS and visual recognition to detect and track underlying patterns, adjusting their trajectory as needed to avoid collisions and ensure the structure's continuity. Real-time experiments using simulated and real-world scenarios validate the efficacy of this proposal.

This research delves into the properties of the Seidel matrix associated with a connected chain graph, examining its eigenvalues, spectral radius, stable range of the Seidel matrix, and the Seidel energy of the graph.

We're investigating a mean-field optimal control issue for stochastic differential equations that incorporate time delays, governed by a fractional Brownian motion with a specific Hurst parameter exceeding 0.5. The dynamics of these delay equations are influenced by a fractional Brownian motion, for which we establish necessary and sufficient stochastic maximum principle conditions to find the optimal control. A key aspect of our research involves deriving explicit yield maximization and consumption optimization strategies in response to a short-term planning horizon.

We've developed a new theory of elliptic finite-band energies for the non-self-adjoint Dirac operator. This involves constructing a non-self-adjoint, elliptic finite-band Dirac operator on a bounded domain in n-dimensional space and establishing the existence of elliptic finite-band Dirac eigenvalues. Furthermore, we've shown that these eigenvalues form a countable, unbounded set. This research generalizes the work of Shatah, Zwanzig, and Kapitanski on the projective metric on invariant subspaces of the Dirac operator.
